Asset.description:
A reusable visual resource referenced by one or more blocks.

Assets are stored once at deck level and referenced by ``uid``. Extraction
is the default and generation is the exception -- reusing the author's own
figures is precisely what separates a domain tool from a generic deck
builder.

path.description: Location of the asset payload on disk.
path.title: Path

latex.description: LaTeX body, for equation assets and Beamer-native tables.
latex.title: Latex

data.description: Structured payload for redrawn charts and tables, so the renderer can emit a native chart object instead of a flat bitmap.
data.title: Data

source_label.description: Label in the source document, e.g. 'Figure 3'.
source_label.title: Source Label

spans.description: Provenance of the asset, required unless authored.
spans.title: Spans

intrinsic_aspect.description: width/height of the asset. Lets the layout engine reserve a correctly shaped hole before the renderer runs.
intrinsic_aspect.title: Intrinsic Aspect

Asset.title: Asset

AssetOrigin.description:
Where a visual asset came from.

For academic use the default must be *extraction*, never generation: an
unattributable decorative image is a liability at a defence. Generated
assets are representable but are flagged by the validator.
AssetOrigin.title: AssetOrigin

Block.description:
The atomic, addressable unit of content.

A block is simultaneously the unit of budgeting, of channel routing, of
click-selection in the preview, and of patching. Keeping all four aligned
on one granularity is what makes natural-language edits deterministic:
a patch names a block ``uid`` and provably cannot disturb anything else.

content.description: Rendered text. LaTeX for equations, source text for code, empty for pure figure blocks.
content.title: Content

bound_to.description: For captions: the sibling block this caption belongs to. Keeps a caption from being separated from its figure by an edit.
bound_to.title: Bound To

needs_confirmation.description: Set by the pipeline when content is inferred or otherwise unsupported. The UI must surface these before export.
needs_confirmation.title: Needs Confirmation

importance.description: Salience used to allocate the duration budget and to decide what degrades to the script channel first.
importance.title: Importance

word_budget.description: Upper bound on rendered length, assigned before drafting. Unit matches the deck's language: CJK characters or English words.
word_budget.title: Word Budget

speaker_note.description: Spoken elaboration for a block that stays on the slide. Distinct from a script-channel block, which has no slide presence at all.
speaker_note.title: Speaker Note

pinned.description: User-protected. Budget rebalancing and automated compression must leave pinned blocks untouched.
pinned.title: Pinned

Block.title: Block

BlockType.description:
Kind of atomic content unit.

A block is the smallest unit that can be independently budgeted, routed to
a channel, patched, or click-selected in the preview.
BlockType.title: BlockType

Channel.description:
Dual-track routing target.

This is the field that implements the "what goes on the slide vs. what the
presenter merely says" split. Both channels are projections of the *same*
content tree, which is what keeps the spoken script and the slides from
drifting apart.
Channel.title: Channel

DeliveryPlan.description:
The talk's timing contract.

This is the input to budget allocation: the pair (duration, density) is
what turns "which content survives" from a matter of taste into an
arithmetic constraint.

total_seconds.description: Target speaking time, excluding Q&A and backup slides.
total_seconds.title: Total Seconds

words_per_minute.description: Speaking rate in budget units per minute. ~200-240 CJK characters/min is typical for rehearsed Mandarin delivery; ~130-150 words/min for English.
words_per_minute.title: Words Per Minute

target_dwell_seconds.description: Preferred seconds per slide. Together with total_seconds this pins the slide count.
target_dwell_seconds.title: Target Dwell Seconds

reserve_ratio.description: Fraction of time held back for overruns and reviewer interruptions. Budgeting to 100% of the clock reliably overruns.
reserve_ratio.title: Reserve Ratio

DeliveryPlan.title: DeliveryPlan

Density.description:
User preference for how much text lands on each slide.

Resolved into concrete numeric caps by
:mod:`rostrum.budget.density`, so downstream code never branches on the
enum directly.
Density.title: Density

Derivation.description:
How a block's text relates to the source document.

Traceability is enforced structurally rather than by prompt instruction:
anything that is not ``AUTHORED`` must carry at least one
:class:`~rostrum.ir.nodes.SourceSpan`, and ``INFERRED`` content is surfaced
to the user for confirmation. In a grant-defence setting a single
fabricated number is fatal, so this is a hard constraint of the schema.
Derivation.title: Derivation

Renderer.description: Target back end. Both consume the identical IR.
Renderer.title: Renderer

Scenario.description: Talk genre. Selects the default rubric profile and section weights.
Scenario.title: Scenario

Section.description:
A logical movement of the talk.

Sections are the unit at which the duration budget is split, and the unit a
rubric checks for completeness -- e.g. a grant defence that never states
its innovation claim is structurally incomplete regardless of how polished
the individual slides are.

weight.description: Relative share of the talk. Deliberately not uniform: for a grant defence, innovation and prior results deserve more airtime than the outline.
weight.title: Weight

rubric_key.description: Which rubric requirement this section discharges, enabling missing-section detection.
rubric_key.title: Rubric Key

intent.description: One-line statement of what this section must achieve.
intent.title: Intent

Section.title: Section

Slide.description:
One page of the deck.

``role`` is the join key against the template's layout catalogue. The
renderer resolves role -> layout -> slot capacities, so the same IR can be
poured into any template that declares the roles it supports.

dwell_seconds.description: Planned time on this slide. Summed across slides this must reconcile with the talk's total duration.
dwell_seconds.title: Dwell Seconds

layout_hint.description: Optional specific layout id, overriding role-based matching. Escape hatch for users who know their own template.
layout_hint.title: Layout Hint

is_backup.description: Reserve slide, excluded from the duration budget.
is_backup.title: Is Backup

Slide.title: Slide

SlideRole.description:
Functional page type.

Template layouts are classified into these same roles, which is how a deck
becomes renderable against an arbitrary user-supplied template: the
renderer matches ``SlideRole`` -> layout, not slide index -> layout.
SlideRole.title: SlideRole

path.description: Original file path or URI, for re-ingestion.
path.title: Path

sha256.description: Digest of the raw input. Lets the tool detect that a source changed underneath an existing deck.
sha256.title: Sha256

char_count.description: Length of the normalised text; bounds all spans.
char_count.title: Char Count

SourceSpan.description:
A pointer back into the ingested source document.

Character offsets refer to the *normalised* source text produced at ingest
time (``SourceDocument.normalized_text``), not to raw bytes of the original
PDF, so that offsets remain meaningful across re-parses of the same input.

doc_id.description: Identifier of the source document this span belongs to.
doc_id.title: Doc Id

start.description: Inclusive start offset into the normalised source text.
start.title: Start

end.description: Exclusive end offset into the normalised source text.
end.title: End

locator.description: Optional human-facing location such as 'p.4' or 'sec:method', used for UI display and for citing back to the author.
locator.title: Locator

quote.description: Verbatim excerpt cached for offline review. Advisory only: offsets are authoritative.
quote.title: Quote

SourceSpan.title: SourceSpan

description:
Root node: a complete, renderer-agnostic presentation plan.

A ``Deck`` is the single source of truth. Slides, the speaker script, the
outline preview and the rubric report are all *projections* of this one
tree, which is why they cannot contradict each other.

template_id.description: Template this deck is currently bound to, if any.
template_id.title: Template Id

targets.description: Renderers this deck is intended for.
targets.title: Targets

rubric_profile.description: Rubric profile id used for completeness checking.
rubric_profile.title: Rubric Profile

title: Deck
